picks.title: More Than $1 Million in Funding Awarded to Teams Building AI Tools for Multilingual Classrooms
picks.take: Multilingual by Design gave $350,000 each to three teams building AI tools for teachers of multilingual students: live transcription of small-group math talk, a tool that chunks and glosses grade-level texts, and a math lesson planner keyed to proficiency levels. Pilots run this year in Wisconsin, Massachusetts and Colorado, so nothing ships to Mississippi yet.
picks.try: Do the Medley move by hand: cut tomorrow's reading into short chunks and add a one-line definition next to each hard word.

picks.title: More CCSD students reach English proficiency, but growth targets plateau
picks.take: Charleston County reported more than 1,400 multilingual students reaching proficiency this year, yet only about 36 percent met their individual growth targets, flat for two years. The district credits a harder academic-language test and 1,700 newcomers, and plans to copy practices from schools that moved up. Mississippi's ELPT accountability points work the same way.
picks.try: Pull your ELs' last two ELPT scores and sort by growth, not level; the flat students are the ones to plan for first.

picks.title: How Schools Can Better Support Older English Learners
picks.take: EdWeek lays out four kinds of secondary ELs (newcomers, long-term, near-reclassification, and dually identified) and what each needs. An Oregon study found fewer than one in five ELs get extra instructional time, and two or more high school years of it raised diploma odds. Chelsea, Massachusetts coaches content teachers to teach language inside their classes.
picks.try: Check one EL's schedule: if the language-support period is costing them English or an elective, raise it with the counselor this week.
